about: Which checks a changed path needs (D-031). A path gets cheaper only when a rule below claims it. Any path no rule claims runs every check: a broad rule is a floor, never a verdict. Control files, which always run everything, are listed in select.mjs; a file that browser specs import runs those specs whatever rule claims it.

proofs.sources: npm run validate && npm run check
proofs.unit: node --test on tests/*.test.js, without the two installer suites
proofs.unit-install: node --test tests/host-install.test.js (Claude Code and Codex installers)
proofs.unit-install-windows: node --test tests/orca-install.test.js (the Orca Windows installer, PowerShell 7)
proofs.build: npm run build && npm run test:dist
proofs.browser: the named Playwright specs in tests/browser, all four projects, plain list reporter
proofs.consumers: npm run ui:consumers && npm run test:ui && npm run ui:report

rules.why: The Claude Code and Codex installers are not part of the site; their own suite proves them.
The Orca Windows installer is not part of the site; its PowerShell suite proves it.
Agent and repository notes are not rendered.
A unit test proves itself; unit tests do not feed the site.
Prose renders on the site: rebuild it and check that it still loads.
One component: its own browser spec, plus the page-wide checks that cover every component.
Ports render on the Ports page and in the downloads: their descriptions, mappings, guides and dist files.
The package is proven by the packed consumers on three engines.
